description: R6 — executable debugger evaluation of a real model (raw base or tuned adapter) on the DISJOINT QuixBugs validation set under the frozen R6 treatment.

timeout_derivation.rule: ONE common pdb_request_timeout_seconds frozen at 60 s (the accepted live-condition r5.1 measurement); reused unchanged for the R6 trajectory generation.

treatment.debugger_entrypoint: target script = task's single writable production path (constraints.allowed_write_paths); disposable fixture copy receives one neutral cwd-safe guarded pytest launcher generated mechanically from task.reproduction.argv. For real-model evaluation, a model-free bounded preflight tries function-scoped structural candidates individually in source order under the exact public reproduction, using a fresh disposable PDB session for each attempted line, and stops at the first reached production line; it consults no verifier, oracle, reference repair, or hidden test content. The adapter fails closed if a model-authored break line is not one of the preflight-proven reachable lines and exposes only the proven line(s) in its bounded corrective retry. The model-authored debugger session remains limited by the common one-session budget. Scripted training transports keep their separately validated real-pausing training breakpoint selection.
treatment.stack_rendering: model-facing stack rendering filtered to frames with script == production path and 1 <= line <= original_source_line_count in EVERY prompt block; raw payload evidence complete.
treatment.model_context: title + description from agent_visible_mapping; original production source; mechanical eligible breakpoint lines; real debugger/tool observations (production-region filtered); SANITIZED reproduction diagnostic; SANITIZED verifier failure records. Verifier retries add only outcome-derived, task-agnostic causal guidance: NO_OP must materially change the reproduced failing path while preserving passing behavior (including the general ordering rule for overlapping predicates); a sanitized candidate runtime exception must be eliminated together with guards enforcing any superseded identity/state/control-flow invariant, and an explicit candidate raise producing that exception plus its controlling conditional must be removed or revised rather than retaining the exception path while swapping construction syntax; other p2p regressions must be narrowed away. Rejected model-authored source is never echoed into a later prompt. No test source, no assertion/literal content, no node ids, no oracle, no reference repair.
treatment.state_machine: accepted R5.9 staged machine: reproduce -> break -> stack -> locals -> step/next -> EITHER stack G2>G1 OR real terminal outcome OR production-exception path -> diagnosis -> bounded PATCH -> PatchManager -> administrative closeout -> EvaluationVerifier. An accepted whole-file 'file' repair correctly advances the adapter to PATCH retry state. Only a retry whose sanitized verifier feedback contains a candidate production exception exposes the unified-diff 'patch' command (plus explicit 'failed'), breaking stateless whole-file regeneration at that causal boundary. Syntax failures and other verifier outcomes retain whole-file recovery.
treatment.patch_serialization: first repair representation: the transport may author the complete corrected file content; the deterministic layer generates the unified diff (difflib, recorded+hashed), then normalizes it. Source-only fail-closed normalization may unwrap an original module plus a complete corrected module embedded as its final string; trim a token-truncated quoted stale-module copy only when the preceding changed module is AST-valid and preserves exactly the original top-level definition names; or restore exact original top-level imports only when a valid materially changed candidate has no imports, preserves exactly the definition set, and loads an original import-bound name. The adapter fails closed before dispatch when a normalized candidate exactly duplicates a previously dispatched verifier-rejected candidate. For parseable whole-file candidates it also records an attribute-free Python AST hash and rejects a candidate whose executable AST duplicates a previously dispatched verifier-rejected whole-file candidate, so comments, formatting, and blank-line variants cannot consume another verifier attempt. After any accepted file or patch repair, retry state is recorded. Candidate-production-exception retries require a model-authored unified diff or explicit failure; syntax failures and non-exception outcomes preserve both whole-file and diff recovery. The existing one-retry budget supplies a non-oracle hard causal instruction without echoing rejected model-authored source. PatchManager and EvaluationVerifier receive the recorded normalized candidate only.
treatment.budget: one common budget (see budgets); no per-task prompt tuning.

source_baseline.note: R6 training data generation; descends from the R6 branch state containing the r5.9 clean-holdout treatment.
